# Calendar

<!-- START TOKEN(Autogenerated block API docs) -->
A calendar of your site’s posts.

- **Name:** `core/calendar`
- **Category:** [widgets](https://developer.wordpress.org/block-editor/reference-guides/core-blocks/core-blocks-widgets/)
- **API Version:** [3](https://developer.wordpress.org/block-editor/reference-guides/block-api/block-api-versions/)
- **Block Type:** [Dynamic](https://developer.wordpress.org/block-editor/getting-started/fundamentals/static-dynamic-rendering/) (server-rendered)
- **Keywords:** `posts`, `archive`

## Block Markup

This is a [**dynamic block**](https://developer.wordpress.org/block-editor/getting-started/fundamentals/static-dynamic-rendering/). It is rendered on the server and does not save HTML in post content.

In post content, it is stored as a block comment:

```html
<!-- wp:calendar /-->
```

## Styling notes

- **Borders** apply to the `table` element (skip-serialized in PHP). Cells inherit border color, style, and width from the table, matching the Table block.
- **Text and background colors** are skip-serialized onto the `table` so month navigation links are not affected.
- **Margin and padding** serialize on the wrapper (`.wp-block-calendar`).
- **Block spacing (`blockGap`)** is skip-serialized and applied as `margin-bottom` on the caption for instance values only. Global Styles block gap is not resolved in the render callback because the Calendar block does not have layout support.

## Testing instructions

1. Insert a Calendar on trunk and on this branch — confirm background still applies to the table/grid only, not nav links.
2. Set border color/width/style on a Calendar instance — border should appear on the table grid, not duplicated per cell.
3. Set a per-side border (e.g. top only) — one line across the top of the grid, not above every row.
4. Set text color — cell borders should follow via `currentColor`.
5. Set margin/padding on the wrapper.
6. Set block spacing — space should appear between the month/year caption and the date grid.
7. Global Styles → Blocks → Calendar: border, text, background, margin, padding.
8. Compare with a theme rule like `td { padding: 8px }` — default calendar cell padding should still apply.
